name: Digit
summary: Inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system for manufacturers and distributors, rebranded from Digit to Sutton in September 2026 (same company, same terms; digit-software.com now redirects to heysutton.com).
best_for: manufacturers and distributors outgrowing spreadsheets who need inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system, and who need lot tracking and traceability rather than just wanting them
skip_if: you are a small operation where $400/month for five users is heavy against what a warehouse module in your existing accounting package would cost; also skip it if your integration list is long, because the per-connection model punishes exactly that: $125 a month for every integration past the second
honest_knock: The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling, and the add-ons are where an inventory system quietly doubles. Two integrations are included, but a working setup usually means an accounting package and a webshop, which is your two, and then Amazon or a second sales channel is another $125 a month (the FAQ and the integrations block agree on that figure since our 22 November 2026 reading). Want the API, or your data inside an AI assistant? $125 a month each. A Starter customer on QuickBooks, Shopify and Amazon with API access is at $650 a month before adding a sixth user. Price the whole configuration you actually need, not the tier.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-11-22 on heysutton.com/pricing, rendered and in the raw HTML; the tier prices have not moved since the 5 September 2026 reading on digit-software.com) Four tiers with three published: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15, and Enterprise on quote. On monthly billing every card reads “then $63/mo each” for extra users, and the FAQ says additional users are $63 per month each. Paying quarterly takes 10% off — $360, $675 and $1,170 a month — and annually 20%, which is $320, $600 and $1,040; the page opens on Monthly, so the first figure you see is the real monthly rate. In the page markup the extra-user price also steps down with the term, $56 on quarterly and $50 on annual billing, while the FAQ only names $63, so which figure applies on a longer term is not confirmed. Two integrations are included on every plan, and the Integrations block now reads “2 integrations included, then $125/mo extra.” That settles the conflict we recorded from September to October 2026, when the same block said $100 while the FAQ said $125. The add-ons cost the same on Starter, Growth and Professional: API access $125 a month, MCP access $125, push notifications and webhooks $63. Customer portals are $18.75 per portal per month on monthly billing, on every tier, Enterprise included, with $17 and $15 alongside it in the markup for quarterly and annual billing. The FAQ adds that implementation and onboarding fees may apply depending on the complexity of the deployment.

compare_with.why: the natural head-to-head for manufacturers leaving spreadsheets. Both cover inventory and production; the difference shows up in how they charge for the edges.
